short: The iconic "Beau Brummell", who established the modern men's suit and defined Regency fashion.
full:
George Bryan "Beau" Brummell rose from middle-class obscurity to become the absolute arbiter of men's fashion in early nineteenth-century London, relying entirely on his immaculate taste, sharp wit, and a close friendship with the Prince Regent. He decisively rejected the ornate, highly decorated clothing of the previous century in favour of understated, perfectly tailored garments.

Brummell popularised the wearing of a dark coat, full-length trousers, a pristine white shirt, and an elaborately knotted cravat, establishing the foundational template of the modern men's suit. His reign as a society dandy ended abruptly when he fell out with the Prince Regent and accrued massive gambling debts, forcing him to flee to France where he eventually died in an asylum.
